plain_english_policy: Enactment of this bill would amend Section 264 of the Alabama Constitution to increase the mandatory retirement age for members of the University of Alabama Board of Trustees from 70 years old to 75 years old. Currently, trustees must vacate their office upon reaching their seventieth birthday; under this amendment, they could serve until their seventy-fifth birthday.
policy_direction_if_enacted: The policy direction is an extension of service eligibility for the University of Alabama Board of Trustees by five years (from age 70 to age 75). This change allows current trustees nearing retirement and future appointees to remain in office longer than previously required under state law.
sponsorship_supports_position: The sponsors affirmatively advanced the bill to increase the age limit for service on the University of Alabama Board of Trustees from 70 years to 75 years.
evidence_quotes: "This bill would propose an amendment... to increase the age limitation for service on the board from 70 years to 75 years."

"The members of the board of trustees as now constituted shall hold office until their respective terms expire under existing law, and until their successors shall be elected and confirmed as hereinafter required." ... "provided however that a trustee shall retire from the board and vacate office at the annual meeting of the board following that trustee's seventieth seventy-fifth birthday."
